newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen Airways to start air cargo service in April.
newsitem.headline: Yemen Airways to start air cargo service in April.

text.p: Yemen's national carrier Yemen Airways will start an air cargo service for the first time in April, an airline official said on Saturday.
"The new unit, which will be named Yemenia Air Cargo, will start operating regular cargo flights for the first time in April," Yehya Sweed, the airline's administrative manager told Reuters.
He said the addition of two Airbus A300s to the airline's fleet in March will expand its operations and make the cargo unit possible.
Sweed did not give details of destinations.
Yemen Airways said in January it will receive two Airbus A300s from manufacturer Airbus Industrie.
The Sanaa-based airline was formed last year by the merger of Yemenia Airways and al-Yemda, the carriers of the former North Yemen and South Yemen which merged in 1990.
Saudi Arabia's national carrier Saudi Arabian Airlines holds a 49 percent stake in Yemen Airways.
The Yemeni airline has a fleet of 12 aircraft-four Boeing 727s, one Boeing 707, three Boeing 737s, three de Havilland Dash-7s and one Airbus A310.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
